summary: London Underground poster claims all Scottish salmon in UK supermarkets comes from factory farms with endemic sea lice and is 'doused in toxic chemicals' including formaldehyde, deltamethrin and hydrogen peroxide, using a gross-out angle against 'gourmet' marketing. It targets general commuters, including children, with a 'Don't Buy It' message.

claims.claim: All Scottish salmon sold in UK supermarkets comes from factory farms
claims.notes: 'All' needs strong proof; some supermarkets sell organic or higher-welfare lines. 'Factory farm' is undefined and contestable.
Lice are widespread and feed on skin/mucus/blood; 'flesh-eating' and 'endemic' need support. No reference doc provided.

claims.claim: Salmon are doused in toxic chemicals including formaldehyde, deltamethrin and hydrogen peroxide
claims.notes: Treatments are licensed and regulated; formaldehyde use and current deltamethrin use in Scotland need verification. 'Doused' implies routine.

claims.claim: Salmon is 'seasoned with a cocktail of chemicals' (implied residues in the food)
claims.notes: Implies chemical residue in the product eaten; a food safety claim needing evidence of residues, otherwise misleading.

claims.claim: They say Scottish salmon is 'gourmet dining'
claims.notes: Attribution to 'they' is vague; identify a real marketing source to show it is a fair characterisation.

attacks.quote: Scandalous scaremongering. Every treatment is licensed, vet-prescribed and strictly regulated, and Scottish salmon is among the safest, highest-standard food in the world.
This implies our fish are laced with poison. There is no residue risk. It's a smear on Scottish farmers and rural jobs.
The ad implies all Scottish salmon contains harmful chemicals and comes from one type of farm. Has the advertiser substantiated 'all', 'toxic' and 'doused'?
Vegan-linked campaign claims your salmon is seasoned with poison; experts say there is no evidence of risk to consumers.
Is my salmon actually unsafe? Or is this just activists scaring people? Now I don't trust either side.
Food safety claims on a mass-audience site carrying health scare content and complaints risk; we need substantiation before approving.

risks.issue: 'All' Scottish salmon in supermarkets is factory farmed: absolute claim, likely unprovable
'Seasoned with a cocktail of chemicals' implies residues in food, a misleading food safety implication
'Toxic', 'doused' and named chemicals presented as routine without dosage, licensing or context; omission risk
Possible disparagement/defamation exposure to the Scottish salmon sector or named supermarket-brand lines (e.g. assured or organic schemes)
'Flesh-eating' and 'endemic' are emotive and need defensible technical support
Health-scare framing may feel like fear-mongering and erode trust among non-vegan target audience
Wall of small text is poor for Underground dwell time and invites scrutiny of detail

fixes.fix: Replace 'All' with a evidenced proportion, or specify the farming system and cite industry/government data on share of production.
fixes.sharpest_defensible_version: 'Almost all Scottish salmon is farmed in crowded sea cages where sea lice thrive.' (only if the data supports 'almost all').

fixes.issue: 'Seasoned with a cocktail of chemicals' implying residues
fixes.fix: Drop the residue implication unless residue data exists; focus on what happens to the fish during farming.
fixes.sharpest_defensible_version: 'Lemon, dill and a lifetime of chemical treatments.' Frames it as the fish's experience, not the food.

fixes.issue: 'Doused in toxic chemicals' and named chemicals
fixes.fix: Verify each chemical's current use in Scottish salmon with sector or regulator data; say 'treated', and state they're used against lice.
fixes.sharpest_defensible_version: 'Scottish salmon are routinely treated with chemicals such as hydrogen peroxide and deltamethrin to fight lice.' (verify; cut formaldehyde unless sourced).

fixes.fix: Use scientifically supported wording and cite a source such as published lice-count or mortality data on the poster.
fixes.sharpest_defensible_version: 'Sea lice eat the skin and flesh of farmed salmon.' Add a source line and lice-prevalence figure if available.

fixes.fix: Prepare an evidence pack with sources per claim, and pre-clear with the poster company and TfL.
fixes.sharpest_defensible_version: Add a small 'Sources: [URL]' line and keep a pre-publication evidence file covering every claim.

working: 'Gourmet dining' versus reality contrast fits the 'Don't Buy It' double meaning.
Lemon and dill 'seasoning' line is a sharp, memorable hook.
Gross-out angle suits a non-vegan audience without asking them to change diet.
Targets a familiar supermarket product, so it is easy to relate to.
legal_flags: Absolute claim ('All') and implied chemical residues in food need documentary evidence under CAP Code rules on misleading advertising; no reference doc supplied to verify.
Possible disparagement/malicious falsehood exposure to the Scottish salmon industry or supermarkets: get a lawyer to review.
Verify each named chemical's actual use in Scottish salmon farming against regulator (e.g. SEPA, VMD) data before publication; none is in the reference pack.
Check TfL advertising policy on health/food safety claims; no TfL policy document was supplied.
